title: ChatGPT export memory and RAG system
description: Build a private local memory layer from exported ChatGPT logs. The system should preserve raw exports, normalize conversations, support keyword and semantic retrieval, expose subject/project browsing, and provide agent-safe tiered memory disclosure.
design: Use multiple memory systems instead of one monolithic store: immutable raw archive, normalized searchable archive, semantic chunk index, curated working memory, and agent-facing retrieval tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap beads exist for ingestion, storage, FTS search, embeddings, hybrid ranking, curated memory, subject browsing, privacy controls, and evals.

title: Define ChatGPT memory schemas and folder contracts
description: Define the on-disk and SQLite contracts for ChatGPT exports before ingestion code lands. Cover raw exports, parsed conversations, chunks, embeddings, curated memories, source links, subjects, and retrieval events.
design: Use immutable raw files under data/chatgpt_exports/raw, normalized JSONL under data/chatgpt_exports/parsed, and SQLite tables for conversations, messages, chunks, memory_records, subjects, embeddings metadata, and retrieval logs.
acceptance_criteria: A spec or design doc defines directories, table names, required fields, indexes, IDs, and migration expectations for the ChatGPT memory system.

title: Implement ChatGPT export ingestion
description: Add a CLI ingestion path for exported ChatGPT data. Parse supported export files into stable conversation, message, and attachment metadata records without modifying the original export.
design: Start with the standard ChatGPT export conversations.json shape. Add parser boundaries so additional export variants can be supported later. Keep raw files immutable and write normalized JSONL plus SQLite records.
acceptance_criteria: lagent ingest-chatgpt --input data/chatgpt_exports/raw imports conversations, preserves source file references, reports counts, is idempotent when run twice, supports --dry-run --trace, writes import_report.json and trace.jsonl under data/logs/<run_id>/, and localizes parse/write errors to stage plus source file or record ID.

title: Build keyword archive search over ChatGPT logs
description: Add fast exact and keyword search over imported ChatGPT conversations so agents and humans can find known phrases, project names, workflows, dates, and titles.
design: Use SQLite FTS5 first. Search should return conversation title, timestamp, role, snippet, source conversation ID, and enough metadata to inspect the original context.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-search "query" returns ranked FTS hits with citations to conversation/message/chunk IDs, supports basic filters for subject, date range, and conversation title, and supports --explain --json with candidate counts, filters, score breakdowns, source kinds, disclosure tiers, and run_id.

title: Add semantic embeddings for conversation chunks
description: Generate and store local embeddings for imported ChatGPT conversation chunks so memory search can find related context even when the query uses different wording.
design: Use the configured local embeddings profile first, likely nomic-embed-text through Ollama. Store embedding metadata in SQLite and keep the vector backend swappable between a simple local store, sqlite-vss, or Qdrant later.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-embed builds embeddings for imported chunks, skips unchanged chunks, records model/version metadata, and exposes clear status when the embedding backend is unavailable.

title: Implement hybrid memory ranking and tiered disclosure
description: Combine keyword relevance, semantic similarity, recency, subject match, and curated memory trust into one inspectable retrieval path. Expose more context only as semantic closeness increases.
design: Use disclosure tiers: far matches expose title/date/one-line summary; medium matches expose relevant chunks; close matches expose surrounding turns and extracted decisions; very close matches expose a wider conversation window and related curated memories.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-search can return a hybrid-ranked result set with explainable scores and a --depth option controlling far, medium, close, and full disclosure.

title: Add curated working memory records
description: Create an explicit, editable memory layer for durable facts agents should trust more than raw chat transcripts. Support project facts, decisions, user preferences, workflows, open loops, and lessons learned.
design: Keep curated memory separate from raw logs. Store records in SQLite with optional Markdown/YAML export so users can inspect and edit them. Promotion should be deliberate, not automatic by default.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-promote can convert a search result or chunk into a typed memory record, lagent memory-show displays it with provenance, and promoted records are included in ranked retrieval.

title: Add subject, project, and workflow browsing
description: Let users and agents browse imported ChatGPT memory by subject, project, workflow type, and time period instead of only searching by query.
design: Start with explicit metadata and lightweight inferred tags. Later clustering can suggest subjects, but user-editable labels should remain authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-subjects lists subjects with counts and recency, lagent memory-search supports subject filters, and imported conversations can be assigned or corrected by subject.

title: Expose agent-facing memory context commands
description: Provide commands local agents can call to retrieve relevant ChatGPT memory with controlled depth and clear provenance.
design: Keep the interface CLI-first before adding daemons or APIs. Output should support Markdown for humans and JSON for agents, with citations back to conversation/chunk/memory IDs.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-context "query" returns ranked context packs with provenance, depth controls, source type labels, and enough metadata for agents to decide whether to inspect more.

title: Add privacy controls and memory audit trail
description: Protect personal ChatGPT exports by default. Track ingestion, retrieval, promotion, and deletion events, and make it clear what content was exposed to an agent.
design: Use local-only defaults, redaction before model calls, immutable raw export provenance, deletions/tombstones for records, and inspectable retrieval logs. Do not send personal memory to external APIs unless explicitly configured.
acceptance_criteria: Memory commands label source types, log retrieval events, support blocking/excluding conversations or subjects, strip obvious secrets before model calls, can show what context was exposed for a run, and integrate with lagent memory-trace <run-id>.

title: Create ChatGPT memory eval fixtures and quality checks
description: Add test fixtures and measurable checks for the memory system so retrieval quality and privacy behavior do not regress as ranking gets smarter.
design: Use synthetic exported conversations covering multiple projects and workflows. Evaluate exact search, semantic recall, subject filtering, tiered disclosure, provenance, and redaction.
acceptance_criteria: python -m pytest covers ingestion/search/ranking behavior, and a lagent memory-eval command or fixture runner reports pass/fail checks for known queries, trace artifacts, memory-check integrity failures, disclosure tiers, provenance, and redaction.

title: Document memory modes and operating model
description: Write the user-facing operating model for the multiple memory systems: raw archive, keyword search, semantic memory, curated working memory, and agent context packs.
design: Document when each memory type should be used, what agents can trust, what remains user-editable, and how disclosure depth changes with semantic closeness.
acceptance_criteria: README or spec docs explain the memory modes, commands, storage locations, privacy defaults, and recommended workflows for project-specific memory browsing.

title: Add memory observability and verification harness
description: Make the ChatGPT memory system inspectable from the terminal before and during implementation. Add trace-first CLI behavior, validation commands, run artifacts, and failure localization so ingestion/search/ranking are not black boxes.
design: Every memory command should emit a run_id, JSON artifacts under data/logs/<run_id>/, and audit rows where relevant. Add dry-run and --trace modes for ingestion, --explain JSON for search/ranking, memory-check for integrity validation, and memory-trace for replaying what happened in a run.
acceptance_criteria: Beads and docs require lagent ingest-chatgpt --dry-run --trace, lagent memory-check, lagent memory-search --explain --json, and lagent memory-trace <run-id>. The contract defines required trace artifacts, validation checks, failure categories, and how errors point to file/record/stage.

title: Catch up the full-history adaptive memory spec
description: Deliver the remaining work needed to turn the full ChatGPT-history memory spec into an implementable local memory substrate. The goal is a staged, inspectable, local-first memory system that can ingest exports, extract candidate memories, retrieve by domain and lens, and evolve through feedback.
design: Treat the spec as Stage 1.5 to Stage 2: lock the ontology first, then implement candidate memory extraction, domain-scoped retrieval, effort-based disclosure, active memory lifecycle, high-risk governance, and end-to-end validation. First release defaults stay conservative; later releases can widen allowances only after the underlying system is proven.
acceptance_criteria: Beads exist for the memory ontology, candidate extraction, scoped retrieval, lens/effort tiers, active memory lifecycle, risk governance, observability, and evals. Each bead has a clear blocking order so implementation can proceed without re-litigating scope. First release behavior remains locked down and conservative by default.

title: Lock the canonical memory ontology and provenance model
description: Define the canonical memory types, reason types, domain list, lens list, temporal validity fields, and provenance rules that all downstream extraction and retrieval code will use.
design: Make the spec executable by pinning the schema for memory records, source links, domain labels, assistant-vs-user provenance, and validity states before extraction logic expands any further. Domain detection may use model assistance, but the canonical labels and policy outputs remain explicit and inspectable.
acceptance_criteria: The repo defines one canonical ontology for domains, memory types, reason types, lenses, and validity states. Assistant suggestions remain distinguishable from user-confirmed memories, and every durable memory has traceable source links and status semantics. Model-assisted domain detection is supported, but its outputs are constrained to the canonical domain set.

title: Extract candidate memories from full ChatGPT history
description: Turn raw ChatGPT exports into reviewable candidate memories with source links, memory types, reason types, domain tags, confidence, and temporal validity metadata.
design: Build the Stage 1.5 ingestion layer that reads transcript history, separates assistant suggestions from user-confirmed outcomes, and emits structured candidates instead of pretending the raw archive is already memory. Assistant suggestions stay in a separate, lower-trust candidate tier until the user explicitly confirms them.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion can produce candidate memories for episodes, facts, preferences, procedures, failures, decisions, open loops, and risks, all linked back to source conversations/messages/chunks. Candidate records are reviewable and do not overwrite the raw archive. Assistant-only suggestions remain segregated from confirmed memory until later-release policies change.

title: Implement domain detection and scoped retrieval
description: Detect the query domain, prefer matching domains, and expand to adjacent domains only under explicit rules. Cross-domain results must be labeled as analogies or transfer, not literal fact.
design: Replace loose subject browsing with a real domain-scoping policy that can steer retrieval across cooking, lab automation, career, finance, health, relationships, and the other initial domains without uncontrolled drift. Use model assistance for domain detection, but keep the final domain labels and expansion rules explicit, bounded, and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Search/context requests choose primary domains, expand only when allowed by effort or explicit request, and label cross-domain results clearly. Domain drift is prevented by policy rather than left to embeddings alone. Model-assisted domain detection is allowed, but outputs must map to the canonical domain list.

title: Add effort tiers, lenses, and contradiction checks
description: Make retrieval choose different depth, lens, and validation behavior at effort levels 1 through 5. The system should expose more context only when the query warrants it.
design: Translate the spec's reflex/basic/structured/deep/exploratory model into concrete retrieval behavior, including graph traversal, temporal checks, contradiction checks, and disclosure expansion.
acceptance_criteria: Retrieval supports explicit effort levels, lens selection, contradiction and temporal checks at higher effort, and explainable disclosure changes from far to full. Higher effort returns more context only when the policy allows it.

title: Implement active memory lifecycle and feedback
description: Add reinforcement, decay, open-loop tracking, and feedback-driven status changes so memory quality improves with use instead of staying static.
design: Store retrieval feedback, source preferences, and freshness signals locally. Use them to reinforce good paths, weaken misleading ones, and surface unresolved open loops for later review.
acceptance_criteria: The system can record positive and negative feedback, update memory status over time, and reflect repeated usefulness or repeated failure in retrieval behavior. Open loops can be promoted, resolved, or deprecated explicitly.

title: Add governance for high-risk domains
description: Treat health, finance, relationships, and similar domains as special cases with stricter temporal validity, source authority, and skepticism rules.
design: Encode the spec's caution layers so high-risk retrieval gets stricter validation, explicit uncertainty, and narrower disclosure than ordinary browsing or recall. Default allowances should stay tightened in the first release and only expand later after the base system proves itself.
acceptance_criteria: High-risk queries are flagged, use stricter source and freshness checks, and never let old or assistant-only suggestions masquerade as current advice or fact. Skeptic review is explicit rather than implied. First-release defaults remain conservative across all allowance knobs.

title: Expand observability and evaluation for the new memory stages
description: Make the new extraction, retrieval, feedback, and governance stages inspectable from the terminal with trace artifacts, validation checks, and regression fixtures.
design: Extend the existing trace-first model to every new memory stage so failures point to a stage, record, source, or policy decision instead of showing up as a black box.
acceptance_criteria: New commands or stages emit run artifacts, trace events, and validation output. The eval suite covers domain drift, assistant-vs-user separation, temporal supersession, disclosure tiers, high-risk governance cases, and conservative first-release defaults.

title: Home MCP for Mac mini
description: Build a self-hosted MCP server on the Mac mini that gives ChatGPT and Codex narrow, auditable access to approved home/project directories and a basic recipe book directory. Start with safe read-only file discovery plus create-only/append-only Markdown note tools, then add remote access plumbing and later expand into memory-backed recipe and household workflows.
design: Treat the Mac mini as the controlled host for external AI clients. The MVP should expose only allowlisted roots, no arbitrary shell, no deletes, and no unrestricted filesystem browsing. Recipe content should land in a simple local recipe book directory first, with hardcoded/structured note-like files that can later be surfaced through the memory system.
acceptance_criteria: A separate epic exists for the Mac mini MCP surface. Child beads define allowlisted roots, path safety, read/search tools, create-only note/recipe write tools, audit logging, and remote access transport. The first release keeps the surface narrow and reversible, and recipe content can be stored locally in a basic recipe book directory for later memory integration.

title: Define Mac mini allowlisted roots and path safety
description: Define the exact writable and readable roots for the home-mcp server on the Mac mini, and enforce path safety so the server cannot escape allowlisted directories.
design: Build a strict allowlist boundary first. No .. traversal, no symlink escape, no hidden-file access unless explicitly enabled, and no filesystem browsing outside configured roots. This is the foundation for every later tool.
acceptance_criteria: The repo documents the allowlisted roots and the server rejects any path outside them. Path normalization is tested, symlink escape attempts fail, and hidden or oversized reads are bounded by policy.

title: Build read-only file discovery and search tools
description: Add read-only file listing, file search, and file read tools scoped to allowlisted roots on the Mac mini.
design: The first tools should let AI discover files, search contents, and inspect notes and recipe documents without write access. Return structured JSON with path, file ID, snippets, and match reasons.
acceptance_criteria: The server can list files, search files, and read files within allowed roots. Results are structured, scoped, and logged, and attempts to search or read outside the configured roots are rejected.

title: Add recipe book directory and note write tools
description: Create a simple local recipe book directory on the Mac mini and add create-only or append-only Markdown note tools for recipes and related household/project notes.
design: Recipe content should be stored as hardcoded, inspectable Markdown notes first, not a complex database. Support create and append flows so AI can save recipe drafts, attempts, and notes safely without arbitrary overwrite or delete behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The server can create and append Markdown notes in the recipe book directory. File names are sanitized, writes are logged, overwrites are avoided by default, and the recipe note format is stable enough to surface later through the memory system.

title: Add audit logging and trace coverage for MCP calls
description: Record every home-mcp tool call with run IDs, inputs, outputs, and failure stages so the Mac mini surface is inspectable from the outside.
design: Every read and write tool should emit trace events and durable logs. Error localization should point to the stage, path, or tool that failed so the system is not a black box when ChatGPT or Codex calls it.
acceptance_criteria: Tool calls produce audit entries and trace artifacts. Failures identify a stage and source path or file ID, and the logs can be inspected later to reconstruct what the AI tried to do.

title: Add remote access transport and authentication
description: Make the Mac mini MCP server reachable to approved outside AI clients through a controlled tunnel or relay with authentication and explicit exposure boundaries.
design: Use a tunnel-based or relay-based transport instead of raw port forwarding. ChatGPT should be able to reach the service, but only through narrow authenticated endpoints and only for the approved tools.
acceptance_criteria: The server is reachable from an external client through the chosen transport. Access requires authentication or equivalent trust gating, and the exposure path is documented and reversible.

title: Bridge recipe book into the memory system
description: Expose the local recipe book directory to the existing memory system later so recipe notes can be searched and promoted alongside ChatGPT transcript memory.
design: Keep this as a later integration step. The recipe book should remain usable on its own first, then a bridge can ingest or index it into the memory stack once the file format and workflow are stable.
acceptance_criteria: A documented path exists for moving or indexing recipe book entries into the memory system later, without changing the primary recipe note workflow or weakening the Mac mini safety boundary.

title: Analyze user input over time
description: Track user prompt behavior over time: semantic density, length, topic distribution, and other metadata that can show how AI usage changes. Keep it separate from the recipe/MCP work for now.
acceptance_criteria:
Can report per-period averages for input length and semantic density.
Can cluster or summarize topics over time.
Can compare recent usage to historical baselines.
Can be added later without changing the current memory/recipe pipeline.

title: Expose memory system to ChatGPT
description: Make the existing local memory stack available to ChatGPT through the approved home-mcp/tunnel path, with narrow tools for read/search/review/promotion and traceable audit logs. Keep this separate from the recipe-book bridge so the memory integration can be built and verified independently.
acceptance_criteria: ChatGPT can reach the memory system through an approved MCP surface or bridge. The exposed tools are narrow, auditable, and role-scoped. Search/review/promote flows remain separate from raw data access. Trace logs show which memory action was invoked and where it failed if a request breaks.

title: Local Agent Lab core CLI and retrieval
description: Cover the core Mac mini coding/search roadmap from the local agent spec: bootstrap, health, models, ask, repo search, repo summarization, log analysis, and eval harness.
design: Keep the first milestone read-only by default, CLI-first, and traceable. Use local retrieval and SQLite-backed indexing before any write workflows widen the surface.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for bootstrap, health/models/ask, indexing/search, summarization, log analysis, and evals. Commands are traceable and default to read-only.

title: Local Agent Lab patch-based editing workflows
description: Cover diff review, patch proposal, function writing, and test writing from the local agent spec.
design: All edits should be patch-first, inspectable, and reversible. No direct overwrite by default.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for review, patch flow, function writing, and test writing. Destructive edits remain gated.

title: Local Agent Lab workspace and agent runtime
description: Cover repo workspace controls, bounded background jobs, local inference helpers, and domain-specific workspace tools from the local agent spec.
design: Use allowlisted repo actions and bounded jobs, not raw shell or unrestricted automation. Keep local inference aligned with the same MCP-style tool boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for repo workspace controls, agent jobs, local inference helpers, and domain-specific tools.

title: Human-memory cognition extensions
description: Cover the human-memory-inspired extensions from the addendum: source monitoring, inhibition, prediction, schemas, salience, prospective memory, consolidation, and retrieval evaluation.
design: Add the highest-value cognition primitives first and keep them cheap, cached, and reviewable. The system should remain local-first and evidence-backed.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for source monitoring, inhibition, person/skill models, prediction/surprise/schemas/counterfactuals, salience/consolidation, and retrieval evaluation.

title: Bootstrap and service scaffolding
description: Set up the initial project structure, config, service startup, and command scaffolding for the Mac mini agent.
design: Make the service bootable and observable before adding any task intelligence. Keep the scaffolding CLI-first and simple.
acceptance_criteria: The repo has startup scaffolding, config loading, and service lifecycle pieces that can run locally without the later agent features.

title: Health, models, ask, and route commands
description: Implement the basic user-facing commands for health checks, available models, direct ask, and task routing.
design: The first command surface should answer what is available, what is healthy, and how a plain-English task gets routed.
acceptance_criteria: lagent health, lagent models, lagent ask, and lagent route exist and produce concise terminal output with logs.

title: Repository indexing and search
description: Build the SQLite-backed repo indexing and hybrid search layer from the local agent spec.
design: Use chunking, symbols, embeddings, and file/path heuristics so the system can find relevant code without needing the whole repo in context.
acceptance_criteria: lagent index-repo and lagent search exist, return ranked results, and persist index metadata and run logs.

title: Repository summarization and prompt packing
description: Add repo summary and context-packing flows for codebases that are too large to inspect all at once.
design: Summaries should be incremental and source-backed, not generic boilerplate. Prompt packing should pull only the minimal useful context.
acceptance_criteria: lagent summarize-repo exists, produces a useful overview, and can feed later code-review or writing tasks.

title: Log analysis workflow
description: Implement the log/error explainer path from the spec.
design: The analyzer should pull stack traces, search referenced code, and distinguish certain causes from speculation.
acceptance_criteria: lagent explain-log exists, handles common traceback formats, and recommends next debugging steps with logs.

title: Eval fixtures and harness
description: Add fixture-driven evaluation for the core local agent workflows.
design: Use repeatable test fixtures so search, review, writing, and log analysis can be measured instead of guessed.
acceptance_criteria: lagent eval exists or an equivalent harness runs the core checks and reports pass/fail artifacts.

title: Diff and file review workflow
description: Implement review over diffs and individual files from the local agent spec.
design: Review should surface bugs, edge cases, missing tests, and risky assumptions without generic style noise.
acceptance_criteria: lagent review works on diffs and file targets, returns actionable comments, and logs the context it used.

title: Patch proposal and apply flow
description: Add patch-first editing primitives for safe multi-file changes.
design: The AI should inspect a proposed patch before applying it, and destructive changes must stay gated.
acceptance_criteria: propose_patch, show_patch, apply_patch, reject_patch, get_git_diff, and revert_last_change are represented in the roadmap.

title: Function writing workflow
description: Implement the small-function writer path from the spec.
design: Generate implementation suggestions and tests first, with apply support only through patch-first flows.
acceptance_criteria: lagent write-function exists conceptually in the roadmap, can inspect nearby code, and produces patchable output.

title: Test writing workflow
description: Implement the test writer path from the spec.
design: The system should inspect the target file and existing tests before proposing new coverage.
acceptance_criteria: lagent write-tests exists conceptually in the roadmap and produces framework-aware test suggestions.

title: Repo workspace controls
description: Add repo selection, status, diff, branch, and commit primitives for workspace-scoped coding.
design: Only allowlisted repos should be visible and writable, with commands mapped per repo instead of arbitrary shell access.
acceptance_criteria: list_repos, select_repo, get_repo_status, get_repo_diff, create_branch, and commit_changes are represented in the roadmap.

title: Bounded agent jobs and background workers
description: Add the bounded background worker model for repo indexing, summarization, and maintenance jobs.
design: Agents should be boring, resumable, cancellable, and logged, not autonomous general-purpose executors.
acceptance_criteria: run_agent, list_agents, get_agent_status, get_agent_result, and cancel_agent_run are represented in the roadmap.

title: Local inference helpers and classification
description: Add local-inference use cases like tagging, summarization, ingredient extraction, duplicate detection, and embedding generation.
design: Local models should reuse the same tool boundary and stay away from security-sensitive or high-stakes decision making.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the local inference surface and its allowed helper tasks.

title: Recipes and baking logs domain tools
description: Add the recipe and baking-log domain tools from the spec as explicit first-class workflows.
design: Recipe and baking knowledge should be preserved as inspectable structured notes with attempts, timelines, and shopping output.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes recipe search, recipe creation, attempt logging, and grocery-list style outputs.

title: Household and project memory tools
description: Add household project, maintenance, inventory, and checklist workflows from the spec.
design: These tools should stay local, note-like, and reversible, with explicit write surfaces instead of implicit automation.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes household project creation, log append, checklist, and project-status flows.

title: Crafts and studio station tools
description: Add craft project, pattern, materials, and attempt tracking from the spec.
design: Craft memory should preserve measurements, materials, and work-in-progress notes as structured local artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes craft project and pattern tooling with appendable notes.

title: Coding project workspace tools
description: Add the coding-project workspace tools and data model from the spec.
design: Repo-scoped coding work should expose patches, tests, task plans, and status through bounded operations only.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes coding project, patch, test-result, and architecture-note tooling.

title: Source monitoring and epistemic metadata
description: Add epistemic status, confidence basis, source reliability, and source-monitoring classification.
design: Candidate memories should be tagged by how they are known, not just by content.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the new epistemic fields and a source-monitoring pass.

title: Inhibition and retrieval gating
description: Add inhibition tags and retrieval suppression for stale, unsafe, or irrelevant memories.
design: Guard retrieval before ranking so stale or assistant-only content does not leak into direct factual answers.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes inhibition tags and an explicit gating pass.

title: Person and skill models
description: Add separate person-model and skill-model tables from the addendum.
design: Keep people and competence separate so preferences, relationship notes, and skill progression do not blur together.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes person models and skill models with source-backed evidence.

title: Prediction, surprise, schemas, and counterfactuals
description: Add schema memory plus prediction, surprise, and counterfactual structures.
design: Useful expectations should be stored separately from raw memories so the system can learn what tends to happen.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes schemas, predictions, and counterfactual memory structures.

title: Affective salience, prospective memory, and nightly consolidation
description: Add affective salience, future triggers, and background consolidation jobs.
design: High-value or emotionally significant memories should get durable retrieval paths, and scheduled consolidation should keep memory current.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes affective salience, prospective triggers, and nightly consolidation behaviors.

title: Retrieval evaluation and background jobs
description: Add eval cases, eval runs, and retrieval verification for the cognition extensions.
design: The new memory primitives should be testable before they are trusted in normal retrieval.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes retrieval evaluation records and background verification jobs.

title: Experimental multi-agent roles and cross-domain exploration
description: Track the later-tier experimental pieces from the addendum: curator, skeptic, analogy, and background exploration roles.
design: Do not build these early; keep them as explicit later-stage work after the substrate and evals are stable.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap contains the experimental later-stage roles and background exploration as deferred work.

title: Memory import pipeline and batch seeding
description: Cover the Stage 1.5 import pipeline: raw export loading, parsing, chunking, domain classification, candidate extraction, deduplication, promotion, entity/link creation, and seed reporting.
design: Keep import boring and batch-oriented. The first pass should process domains incrementally and leave clear traces at every stage.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for parsing, domain classification, candidate extraction, dedupe/canonicalization, promotion, entity/link creation, and seed reports.

title: Memory retrieval, context compiler, and effort tiers
description: Cover the retrieval engine and context compiler from the memory spec: scoring, domain drift control, effort levels, context packet generation, and disclosure tiers.
design: Treat retrieval as an evidence pipeline, not just search. Each step should be inspectable and should explain why memory was included or excluded.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for retrieval scoring, context compilation, effort tiers, and domain drift control.

title: Memory lifecycle and active reinforcement
description: Cover the active-memory system: reinforcement, penalization, open loops, consolidation, supersession, and ongoing memory maintenance.
design: This is the “memory gets better by use” layer. Keep it explicit and reviewable so it does not become hidden self-modification.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for reinforcement, open loops, nightly consolidation, supersession, and memory lifecycle updates.

title: Memory UI, reporting, and evaluation surfaces
description: Cover the user-facing and QA surfaces from the memory spec: import UI, candidate review UI, retrieval lab, open loops, seed report, and eval harness.
design: Make the system inspectable from outside the black box. The UI/reporting layer should show what the memory system thinks it did and why.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for the UI pages, seed reports, eval cases, and performance visibility.

title: Memory provider abstractions and performance guardrails
description: Cover LLM provider abstraction, embedding provider abstraction, and the Mac-mini performance strategy for the memory system.
design: Keep the system model-agnostic and cheap by default. Small jobs should use small models; heavy jobs should be cached or queued.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for model abstraction, embedding abstraction, review queues, and latency/performance constraints.

title: Memory import parsing and chunk structures
description: Parse ChatGPT exports into raw conversations, messages, and chunks with stable IDs and source provenance.
design: This is the parser/normalization bedrock for everything else. It needs to be repeatable and batch-safe.
acceptance_criteria: The import parser, chunking, and stable-ID behavior are represented in the roadmap.

title: Memory candidate extraction and canonicalization
description: Extract candidate memories from imported chunks and deduplicate/normalize them into canonical memory objects.
design: The system should separate candidate extraction from promotion and keep assistant suggestions clearly distinguishable until confirmed.
acceptance_criteria: Candidate extraction, dedupe, and canonicalization are represented in the roadmap.

title: Memory retrieval scoring and domain drift control
description: Implement the scoring formula, hard filters, soft penalties, and domain drift controls for memory retrieval.
design: Retrieval should prefer relevant and current memories, suppress stale or risky ones, and label cross-domain transfer explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring, filtering, and domain-drift behavior are represented in the roadmap.

title: Memory context packet compilation
description: Build the context packet compiler that packages retrieved memories, warnings, source IDs, and disclosure tiers for agents.
design: Context compilation should produce a small evidence packet rather than a transcript dump.
acceptance_criteria: Context packet generation and evidence packaging are represented in the roadmap.

title: Memory open loops and consolidation jobs
description: Add open-loop tracking and nightly consolidation work for the active memory system.
design: The system should remember unresolved questions and periodically consolidate, decay, and update memory maintenance artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Open loops and consolidation are represented in the roadmap.

title: Memory UI pages and seed report
description: Build the memory UI/reporting surfaces and the seed report output from the spec.
design: The system should make import, candidate review, retrieval lab, and seed reporting visible to the user.
acceptance_criteria: The UI pages and seed report are represented in the roadmap.

title: Memory evaluation cases and high-risk domain tests
description: Add the concrete eval cases for cooking, drift, analogy, stale context, health, finance, and relationship queries.
design: The spec’s example queries should become actual tests so the system can prove it is behaving conservatively.
acceptance_criteria: The example queries and high-risk eval cases are represented in the roadmap.

title: Model routing and escalation labels
description: Implement the model router and explicit escalation labels from the local agent spec.
design: Route code review, function writing, and tests to the coding model; summaries to the fast summarizer; ask/routing to the chat model; and make escalation explicit when the task is above the local model’s weight class.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes model routing and escalation labels for task types and context size.

title: Prompt library and prompt contracts
description: Store the required task prompts as markdown files and keep their output contracts explicit.
design: Prompts should live in config/prompts and specify the expected response shape for review, function writing, and narrow search.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes prompt files and their structured output requirements.

title: Shell wrapper policy and command allowlist
description: Implement the shell wrapper and blocked-command policy from the local agent spec.
design: Default to a conservative allowlist with explicit blocks for destructive or install-style commands.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes shell command boundaries and the default blocked list.

title: Run logging and artifact layout
description: Implement the run logging and artifact layout for all local agent commands.
design: Every run should record prompt, context, model, output, and timing in data/logs with a reproducible folder layout.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the command log schema and artifact directory layout.

title: Redaction and secret-safety guardrails
description: Implement the context redaction rules before anything is sent to a local model.
design: The system should strip .env and common secret patterns before model calls and never include secret files in prompts.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the redaction rules and secret-safety policy.

title: SSH-first bootstrap and environment setup
description: Implement the SSH-first bootstrap commands and setup checklist for a fresh Mac mini.
design: The bootstrap should check Homebrew and core tools, create project directories, and keep system changes reversible.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the bootstrap script, setup commands, and first-run checklist.

title: Configuration and justfile command surface
description: Implement the config file and justfile command shortcuts from the local agent spec.
design: The CLI should have predictable shortcuts and a single YAML config source for paths, model names, retrieval limits, and safety flags.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the config schema and justfile shortcuts.

title: Eval fixture repos and deterministic checks
description: Build the fixture repos and deterministic checks for review, search, and log analysis.
design: Each fixture should encode one class of bug or search target so evals prove the agent is better than blind prompting.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes fixture repos, expected behavior, and deterministic eval outputs.

title: Candidate extraction prompt and validation
description: Implement the candidate extraction prompt and structured output validation from the memory spec.
design: The extractor should produce bounded candidate memories with the required schema and should fail safely when the output is malformed.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the extraction prompt and validation step for candidate memories.

title: Context compiler prompt and packet schema
description: Implement the context compiler prompt and output packet requirements from the memory spec.
design: The compiler should assemble a small evidence packet with sources, warnings, and disclosure-aware sections.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the context compiler prompt and context packet schema.

title: High-risk domain handling
description: Implement the high-risk domain rules for health, finance, relationships, and legal queries.
design: The system should apply caution flags, staleness penalties, and stricter review when domains are sensitive.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the high-risk domain handling rules and caution behavior.

title: Memory project structure and package layout
description: Align the package and directory structure with the memory spec’s implementation layout.
design: The codebase should keep import, retrieval, UI, and eval responsibilities separated cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the memory project structure and layout expectations.

title: LLM provider abstraction
description: Add the model-provider abstraction so the memory system can swap LLM backends without redesign.
design: The system should keep the model interface narrow and support local-first execution with optional future providers.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes LLM provider abstraction.

title: Embedding provider abstraction
description: Add the embedding-provider abstraction so vector backends can change without changing public IDs.
design: The system should separate embedding generation from storage and keep model metadata explicit.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes embedding provider abstraction.

title: Memory UI shell and review pages
description: Add the memory UI shell and the core review pages from the spec.
design: The UI should make import, candidate review, retrieval lab, and open-loop review visible without turning into a black box.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the memory UI pages and the review shell.

title: Memory seed report generation
description: Add the seed report generation and markdown export from the memory spec.
design: The seed report should summarize domains, candidates, approved memories, patterns, and stale or contradictory items.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the seed report output.

title: Private personalized search layer
description: Cover the future private search module from the local agent spec: metasearch, local indexing, source preferences, query memory, and iPhone access.
design: This should stay local-first and transparent, with editable ranking rules and no attempt to build a full public web index.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for metasearch, local indexing, query/source memory, iPhone access, and the search API.

title: Metasearch and local search API
description: Implement the metasearch and local search API surface for the private personalized search layer.
design: Blend public web discovery with local document and saved-page indexing behind a simple local API.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes metasearch and a local search API.

title: Query memory and source preference storage
description: Add query history, source preferences, and feedback storage for the private search layer.
design: Keep ranking signals local and inspectable so the system can learn from usage without becoming opaque.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes query memory, source preferences, and feedback storage.

title: iPhone access and capture workflows
description: Add the iPhone-facing query and capture workflows for the private search layer.
design: The mobile workflows should support query submission, page saving, and result feedback through the same local backend.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the iPhone access and capture flows.

title: Local dashboard for search and memory surfaces
description: Implement a simple local dashboard for the search and memory surfaces.
design: Keep the GUI light and inspectable: recent runs, search interface, review outputs, and patch previews.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap includes the optional GUI/dashboard surfaces.

title: Home MCP note discovery and project helper tools
description: Add the next narrow Home MCP capability batch from the scope spec: Markdown note search, recent file listing, direct recipe retrieval, recipe attempt comparison, and create-only project notes.
design: Reuse the existing allowlisted roots, Markdown note writer, recipe parser, JSON-RPC dispatcher, CLI command pattern, and trace/log artifacts. Keep the project note flow create-only under the projects root and keep recipe comparison read-only.
acceptance_criteria: MCP tools and matching CLI commands exist for search_notes, list_recent_files, get_recipe, compare_recipe_attempts, and create_project_note. Tests cover happy paths, root rejection for get_recipe, JSON-RPC dispatch, and project note root scoping.

title: Baking observation camera workstations
description: Build camera workstations for sourdough, proofing, and baking observation using the Raspberry Pi/Arducam path first, then ESP32-S3 stations later.
design: Keep v0 still-image only, trace-first, and locally inspectable. Use the Pi as the primary path; do not block v0 on ESP32 firmware or live video.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for storage/session schema, Pi SSH/camera health, still capture, scheduled capture, sync/indexing, recipe integration, Home MCP exposure, ESP32 evaluation, and later AI observation.

title: Define baking observation storage and trace schema
description: Define the on-disk session/capture layout, device metadata, capture IDs, and run trace artifacts for baking observation workflows.
design: Use docs/baking_observation_workstations.md as the contract. Keep capture metadata sidecar JSON files plus a future SQLite index so v0 works before database implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Storage paths, session fields, capture metadata fields, trace stages, and failure categories are documented and reflected in CLI tests or fixtures.

title: Implement Pi SSH and camera health checks
description: Add a health command for the Raspberry Pi camera workstation at dave@DavesDev.
design: Check SSH connectivity, hostname/time, disk space, camera tooling availability, and whether at least one Arducam/camera device is visible. Return structured status with stage-specific errors.
acceptance_criteria: lagent bake-cam health --device DavesDev reports SSH, camera availability, disk space, and time sync enough to debug failures from the Mac mini terminal.

title: Capture one still image from the Pi workstation
description: Implement capture-now for a single still image from the Raspberry Pi/Arducam workstation.
design: Start with SSH-executed camera capture and copy the resulting image back to the Mac mini. Write sidecar metadata and a trace for each stage.
acceptance_criteria: lagent bake-cam capture-now --session <id> --device DavesDev --camera main creates an image and metadata under data/baking_observations/sessions/<session_id>/captures and reports a run_id.

title: Sync and index baking capture artifacts
description: Make capture artifacts browsable and safely synchronized from camera devices to the Mac mini.
design: Maintain latest image links/copies, sidecar JSON metadata, and a small index reader before adding any heavier database dependency.
acceptance_criteria: lagent bake-cam sync, latest, list-sessions, and show-session can prove what was captured, where it lives, and whether any upload failed.

title: Add scheduled t-plus capture plans
description: Support schedules for sourdough starter feedings, bulk fermentation, final proofing, and bake observation.
design: Represent schedules as t+elapsed capture plans tied to a session start time. Implement deterministic plan generation before background scheduling automation.
acceptance_criteria: A starter feeding session can define captures like t+0h, t+2h, t+4h, t+8h, and the system can show pending/done/missed captures.

title: Add terminal status views for baking observation
description: Expose lightweight terminal views so baking camera sessions are not a black box.
design: Provide concise CLI status output first: devices, active sessions, last capture, failed stage, next scheduled capture, and latest image path.
acceptance_criteria: A single command shows current baking observation health, active sessions, latest capture paths, and recent failures without needing browser or manual SSH inspection.

title: Attach baking capture sessions to recipe attempts
description: Connect observation sessions to recipe cards and attempts so captured proofing/baking evidence can become structured recipe history.
design: Keep recipe note files as source of truth. Add explicit links from recipe attempt metadata to capture session IDs; do not auto-promote visual observations to memory yet.
acceptance_criteria: A recipe attempt can reference one or more baking observation session IDs, and recipe tooling can list linked captures for that attempt.

title: Expose baking observation through Home MCP
description: Add MCP tools for starting/listing baking observation sessions and retrieving latest still images.
design: Expose minimal create/read actions after the CLI is stable: start session, latest image, list sessions, show session. Keep permissions narrow and rooted under baking observation storage.
acceptance_criteria: Browser ChatGPT can start a baking observation session, ask for the latest still image metadata, and list session status through Home MCP without direct shell access.

title: Evaluate ESP32-S3 still camera workstation path
description: Evaluate whether the ESP32-S3 boards should become secondary still-image camera workstations.
design: Do this only after the Pi capture/sync path works. Compare capture quality, reliability, upload approach, power, and firmware maintenance burden.
acceptance_criteria: A short decision record recommends ESP32-S3 use cases, firmware approach, and whether it belongs in v1 or later.

title: Plan local AI observation over baking image sequences
description: Design the later AI layer that observes proofing/baking image sequences and summarizes visual changes.
design: Do not implement model judgment until image capture, metadata, recipe linkage, and human review are reliable. Start with read-only summaries and explicit uncertainty.
acceptance_criteria: A future design defines image sequence inputs, model routing, observation output schema, uncertainty labels, and how observations are kept separate from confirmed recipe facts.

title: Resilient baking camera transport fallback
description: Add a fallback transport strategy for baking camera workstations when Tailscale/Wi-Fi SSH is intermittent in the device location.
design: Keep the current SSH/Tailscale path as primary. Add an offline-first device spool and evaluate Bluetooth or nearby-device relay for status/capture metadata and delayed image transfer. Do not require live video over Bluetooth.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap covers retry policy, local spool on the Pi, delayed sync, failed-transfer recovery, and a decision on Bluetooth/Nearby relay feasibility with a small smoke test.
